title: Best Creative Testing Agencies for Meta Ads (2026)
summary: Compare seven creative testing agencies for Meta ads by testing method, monthly volume, published pricing and who runs the ads. Facts checked October 2026.
body_markdown:
Our top pick is Knowlify, for brands that want weekly batches of AI video ads, with or without Meta campaign management. A creative testing agency for Meta ads keeps new Facebook and Instagram ads flowing into your account, tests them in a controlled way and turns the results into the next brief. Among the alternatives, the right one depends on whether the agency should also run media, whether you already have a media buyer, and whether you need a price before a call. As of October 2026, MetaAdsAgency, Pilothouse and Brill Media pair testing with media buying, inBeat and Ecom Republic plan creative around a testing roadmap, and TubeScience and MediaNug suit teams that run their own ads.


**Disclosure and method.** Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared. Our UGC-style ads use AI presenters rather than human creators, which matters when you compare agencies that work with real creators. Every fact about another provider comes from that provider's own website, checked on October 26, 2026. We have not hired these agencies, so this is a comparison of published scope, not a test of results. Confirm prices and terms on each provider's page before you sign.


## What does a creative testing agency do for Meta ads?


It runs a loop: write a hypothesis, produce ads that differ in one meaningful way, launch them so each gets a fair read, decide what to scale or stop, and brief the next round from the result. Our[ad creative testing framework](https://knowlify.com/articles/ad-creative-testing) shows how to design those tests yourself. This guide covers who you can hire to run the loop.


Meta supplies the mechanics. Its Marketing API[split testing documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/guides/split-testing/) describes tests on mutually exclusive audiences, advises one variable per test, and includes a creative test type that compares 2 to 7 cells with exactly one ad in each. It also notes that tests with larger reach, longer schedules or higher budgets tend to give more statistically significant results, so plan a budget for testing.


Meta also expects more creative in its systems. Its[Andromeda engineering post](https://engineering.fb.com/2024/12/02/production-engineering/meta-andromeda-advantage-automation-next-gen-personalized-ads-retrieval-engine/) (December 2024) says the retrieval stage narrows tens of millions of candidate ads to a few thousand and that the number of ad creatives in its systems is expected to grow significantly. Meta's[Advantage+ creative](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/meta-advantage-plus/creative) page says the tools use AI to generate and enhance ad variations across image, video and carousel formats, from your existing assets or from scratch. Deciding which customer problem, angle or proof to test, and turning results into the next brief, is the work an agency is hired for.


Testing is ongoing because winners wear out, as our[creative fatigue guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/creative-fatigue) explains.


## How we chose and compared these agencies


We included currently operating providers that name Meta (Facebook or Instagram) on their own site and describe a testing method, favoring those AI answers already cite for this question. We compared testing method, volume, published price and who runs the ads. Knowlify, our top pick, is listed first; we did not rank the others, and the table groups each provider by the job it fits.

## Knowlify: our top pick for weekly AI video ads to test on Meta


Knowlify is our top pick for brands that want a steady weekly supply of new ads to test. Knowlify (YC S25), which publishes this guide, is a done-for-you AI ads agency for Facebook and Instagram. We make AI UGC, 3D character animation and AI commercial video ads, about 25 finished ads a week (about 100 a month) in weekly batches. Our team writes the scripts, and a person checks every ad before delivery. You can choose end-to-end Meta ads, where we make the creative and manage campaigns in your own Meta ad account, or creative-only if you have a media buyer. You keep the ads. Pricing is a custom quote on a[30-minute call](https://knowlify.com/book) , the first batch arrives five days after kickoff, and there is a 90-day guarantee (terms on knowlify.com). Public ads we made for Parva and Casco are in our[Facebook video ad examples](https://knowlify.com/articles/facebook-video-ad-examples) .


Knowlify is not the right fit when:


- **You need real people on camera.** Our UGC-style ads use AI presenters, not human creators. For creator-led tests or partnership ads, TubeScience, Ecom Republic or Pilothouse are closer matches.
- **You want a published price first.** MetaAdsAgency is the only provider here that lists its fees.
- **You test across many platforms.** Knowlify focuses on Facebook and Instagram. inBeat lists several other platforms.
- **You want a testing roadmap as the main deliverable.** inBeat, Brill Media and MediaNug each describe a documented framework.


## Which agencies run creative testing and media buying together?


These three make or source the ads and also run the campaigns.


### MetaAdsAgency: flat plans with a written verdict per test


As of October 2026, MetaAdsAgency describes itself as an independent Facebook and Instagram ads agency, not affiliated with Meta. Its creative testing page says it tests one variable at a time (angle, hook, format or offer) in a separate testing campaign with its own budget, waits for enough conversions or a clear early signal from hook rate and click-through rate, and ends each test with a written verdict to scale, iterate, hold or retire, logged in a client portal.


Its[pricing page](https://metaadsagency.com/pricing) , checked October 26, 2026, lists Growth at $2,400 a month billed yearly ($3,000 billed monthly) for ad spend up to $50,000 a month, with 12 new creatives and 2 UGC-style videos a month. Scale is $4,800 a month billed yearly for spend up to $150,000 with 30 new creatives, and Enterprise is $9,600 a month billed yearly above that with 60. There is no setup fee or percentage of spend, and ad spend is paid directly to Meta. The[MetaAdsAgency homepage](https://metaadsagency.com/) says it works as a partner inside your own Business Portfolio and that its plans are built for brands spending $20,000 a month and more.


**Consider it when** you want a published price, a fixed monthly creative count and one team for creative and media.


### Pilothouse: testing inside a DTC Meta program


As of October 2026, Pilothouse's Meta ads page lists static, motion and UGC concepts, volume and variation pipelines, and hook, story and offer testing across feeds, Reels and Stories, next to active media buying with an Advantage+ campaign mix, landing pages and reporting. It lists 500+ DTC brands served, and its footer lists an address in Victoria, British Columbia. Its blog describes a[3-3-3 testing framework](https://www.pilothouse.co/post/meta-creative-testing-framework-the-3-3-3-approach-to-finding-winners) : three funnel levels, three angles and three formats, tested in equal-budget ad sets before winners move into Advantage+ sales campaigns. A separate[Pilothouse Studios](https://www.pilothouse.co/studios) page lists ad creative, creator content and videography. Pricing is not published.


**Consider it when** you run a DTC brand and want testing, media buying and landing pages with one agency.


### Brill Media: a fixed framework on a 3 to 4 week cycle


Brill Media's creative testing page, checked October 26, 2026, lays out a specific Meta routine: split 5 ads into 15 assets (headlines, images or videos, and primary text), run a 2-day control and variable test, run dynamic creative with the winners for 2 to 3 weeks (20 combinations or fewer), then move winners into a "proving ground" campaign, adding a new winning ad each month. It says you repeat the cycle every 3 to 4 weeks and that it works for B2B, B2C, ecommerce, retail and lead generation advertisers. It lists a dedicated account team and an office in Encino, California. Pricing is not published.


**Consider it when** you want a testing routine you can understand up front, run by an agency that also buys media.
